Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroSolar Renewables third quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your telephone keypad if you would like to ask a question. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss AeroSolar Renewables' results for the third quarter. Joining me on today's call are Jordan Hayes, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Development Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Technology Officer; Emma Rodriguez, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Tom Keller, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hayes.

Jordan Hayes:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. AeroSolar Renewables delivered exceptional results in the third quarter, showcasing our leadership in the renewable energy sector. Our success is attributable to our innovative technologies, strategic partnerships, and unwavering commitment to sustainability.

Today, I want to highlight seven key aspects of our performance:

1. On construction progress and commercial operation dates, our development backlog remains a cornerstone of our growth story at AeroSolar Renewables, standing at 12.4 GW across utility-scale solar PV, onshore and offshore wind, battery energy storage systems—or BESS—and our emerging green hydrogen portfolio. This strong position enables us to deliver more than 3 GW of new capacity online in 2025 alone, supported by a weighted average internal rate of return of 12.8% and long-term power purchase agreements averaging 15 years at competitive strike prices under $35 per MWh for solar and $50 per MWh for wind, enhanced by production tax credits and investment tax credits from the Inflation Reduction Act.

Diving into progress by asset class and region, focusing on our top 10 projects that make up 85% of the backlog, our 2.8 GW solar pipeline is advancing strongly, with overall construction at 68% complete by the end of Q3—up from 52% a year ago, due to faster engineering, procurement, and construction mobilization and resolution of supply chain issues for TOPCon and next-generation HJT modules.

In the U.S. Southwest, the 550 MWdc Desert Peak Solar project in Arizona reached 92% mechanical completion last month, with Sungrow string inverters fully operational. Bifacial PERC-plus modules at 23.5% efficiency are exceeding nameplate expectations, with DC:AC ratios at 1.35:1 to reduce clipping losses. Commercial operation date holds steady for Q4 2024, matching our $480 million investment and a 20-year PPA with APS at $28 per MWh, including 30% ITC bonuses for domestic content.

The 400 MWac Lone Star Solar cluster in Texas progressed to 75%, using Enphase IQ8 microinverters for better grid stability in ERCOT's variable conditions. We've overcome permitting challenges tied to transmission upgrades, shifting COD slightly to Q1 2025—30 days later than before—but without capital expenditure overruns, as steel costs have stabilized after Ukraine-related disruptions.

U.S. solar construction is progressing twice as fast as in Europe thanks to IRA benefits, while we're balancing with 500 MW in development in Australia's National Electricity Market, where hybrid rooftop-to-utility setups are surging with coal plant retirements.

For offshore wind, our 4.2 GW portfolio—our top-margin area at 14.2% IRR—is 41% complete, a 15-point year-over-year gain from pre-assembled jacket foundations and Vestas V236-15.0 MW turbines. Floating offshore technology sets us apart, targeting levelized cost of energy below $60 per MWh.

The lead 850 MW Atlantic Horizon off New Jersey is 55% done, with monopile piling 85% finished using DEME's Orion vessel, similar to Orsted's Hornsea approach. Turbine installs start Q1 2025, aiming for full COD in the second half of 2026 per updated BOEM schedules. We've locked $1.2 billion in tax equity from Macquarie, expecting capacity factors over 55% with optimized wake layouts.

In Europe, the 600 MW Nordsee Breeze floating project in Germany's North Sea is at 35%, partnering with Equinor on DeltaWind semi-submersibles. Supply issues with Siemens Gamesa blades, reminiscent of Orsted challenges, delayed COD to Q3 2026, but fixed-price EPC from Van Oord at $800 million, plus REPowerEU grants covering 40% of capex, has de-risked it.

Ongoing issues like 20% higher global vessel rates persist, but forward contracts secure 85% of turbines, avoiding Siemens gearbox problems.

Our 3.5 GWh BESS backlog is 72% complete, capitalizing on CAISO and ERCOT opportunities with 92% round-trip efficiencies from CATL and EVE LFP packs.

The 1.2 GWh GridForge in California is 88% along, with power conversion system commissioning via Fluence's Gridstack. COD moves to Q4 2024 due to electrolyte delays, but we're securing $150 per kWh from resource adequacy contracts and ancillaries, at 18% returns.

Overseas, the 500 MWh expansion of Australia's Hornsdale Power Reserve—building on Tesla's model—is 65% done, targeting Q2 2025 COD to aid AEMO frequency control amid over 15% rooftop solar curtailments.

Green hydrogen's 200 MW electrolyzer pipeline is 22% advanced, emphasizing alkaline-PEM mixes for steady offtake. The 100 MW HydroPure in Rotterdam's port is 40% on foundations, with ITM Power stacks incoming. COD mid-2026 aligns with EU Hydrogen Backbone and $500 million IPCEI support, aiming $2.50 per kg at 60% load via co-located solar feedstocks.

In total, 65% of the pipeline is in construction, versus 48% last year, with $2.1 billion capex deployed year-to-date—10% under budget from steel and polysilicon drops of 25% quarter-over-quarter. Risks like NEPA permitting and queues are managed with 90% queued MW under MISO/PJM updates and $450 million from divesting 300 MW early assets.

Forward, 4.2 GW CODs in 2025-2026 should lift EBITDA 35% to $1.8 billion, with DCF upside of $2 per share per 100 MW faster delivery. Tech like 25%+ HJT solar, 15 MW turbines, and 8-hour BESS positions LCOE under $20 per MWh by 2030, competitive with NextEra and Iberdrola.

2. Turning to storage deployment and hybrid project updates, before financial details, these are vital growth engines at AeroSolar Renewables. Storage ensures renewable scalability for grid reliability, tackling intermittency and opening ancillaries and capacity revenues. Hybrids, like solar-plus-storage and wind-plus-storage, speed up via Inflation Reduction Act ITC/PTC modifiers boosting our U.S. pipeline.

In Q3, we hit first energy on 450 MW / 1,800 MWh from three standalone BESS, lifting operational storage to 2.3 GW / 9.2 GWh year-to-date—180% above Q3 2023. Highlights include Horizon Valley in ERCOT: 200 MW / 800 MWh four-hour LFP at 92% efficiency via our AetherFlow software, beating 89% goals. Early results: $45 per MWh arbitrage in summer peaks, plus $12 per MWh from real-time frequency regulation.

Deployment ramps with $3.2 billion backlog for 4.8 GW / 19 GWh through 2026. Vertical integration secures 85% offtake in 15-year PPAs/tolling with Google, Southern California Edison. New storage PPAs average $28 per kW-month, up 12% year-over-year amid supply stabilization and $12,000/tonne lithium.

U.S. is 70%, California leading with 650 MW / 2.6 GWh under Storage Initiative. ERCOT's 1.2 GW leverages SB8 changes. Australia adds 300 MW / 1.2 GWh yielding 25% IRRs in FCAS like Fluence's New England. UK: 150 MW / 600 MWh in Balancing Mechanism at £25/kW-year T-4 premiums.

Tech pushes include iron-air LDES pilot from Form Energy at 50 MW / 1,300 MWh in PJM for 100+ hour discharge. Nexus VPP aggregates 1.5 GW, lifting uncontracted revenue 22% via AI stacking. Degradation under 1.5% yearly per DNV.

Hybrids are 55% of 12 GW pipeline, up from 35%, de-risking queues. 1.1 GW operational/under construction: Mojave solar-storage (400 MWdc + 160 MW/640 MWh), ops in May, PG&E PPA $55/MWh blended, 98% solar capture, 35% value from peaks.

Texas Panhandle wind-storage (350 MW Vestas V150-6.0 MW + 140 MW/560 MWh), 75% complete for Q4 COD, JPMorgan tax equity with 45X PTCs, 85% capacity factor equivalent vs. 15% curtailment.

Chile Atacama 250 MWp solar + 100 MW/400 MWh, Corfo/EDF backed at $65/MWh, eyeing sodium-ion.

Hybrids bridge to 24/7 power, LCOE $32/MWh by 2026 per NREL models. We match NextEra's 1.9 GW backlog. Hedged 70% 2025 cells from LG/BYD despite 8% QoQ rise. FERC 2023 shaves queues.

Storage/hybrids: 28% Q3 revenue $420 million, 62% EBITDA margins via $4.5/kW-year O&M. $1.1 billion capex on track. FY24: 3.5 GW deployments (60% hybrids/storage), 5 GW 2025 with $4.5 billion debt. Transformative for 15-18% CAGR, capturing BNEF's 100 GWh global pace.

3. On tax equity financing and project-level financing, these are essential for scaling our 5.2 GWp pipeline in solar PV, onshore wind, and BESS, de-risking the balance sheet and maximizing IRA incentives in high-rate times.

Tax equity, 35% of Q3 funding, draws banks like JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Google, Amazon for ITCs/PTCs. IRA stacks 30% base ITC with 10% domestic/10% energy community, hitting 50%+.

Q3 closed $850 million in two deals. $450 million flip for 400 MWdc SunVista in ERCOT (LONGi TOPCon, Nextracker trackers): bank takes 99% ITC/cash to 7-8% IRR in 3-4 years, then we get 95% residuals at 15-18% IRRs. Priced 6.5% yield vs. 8% prior.

$400 million true-up for 300 MW WindRidge in SPP Oklahoma (Vestas V150-4.2 MW, 45%+ factors): monetizes 45X on components + $27/MWh PTCs. Demand up 25% YoY from NOLs, closes in 4-6 weeks.

U.S. 85%, piloting Europe CfD/EEG. Keeps leverage 2.5x vs. NextEra 3.8x, recycled $200 million sponsor equity.

Project debt: 60/30/10 stack's 60%, $1.2 billion Q3 at LIBOR+175 bps (5.75% fixed). $650 million for 250 MW/1 GWh Horizon in CAISO (Tesla Megapack, PG&E $45/MWh), 65% advance, 1.45x DSCR.

$550 million Mojave 500 MWdc in PJM (Dominion PPA 16.2% P90 IRR), LC facility, Fluor security. Rates up 50 bps, but competitive.

Tight banks shift to KfW for turbines (20% draws). Pay-go cuts contingencies 15%. Australia A$300 million bonds at 6.2%.

Optimizes hurdles to 12-15% amid LCOE falls. $3.5 billion queued 2025, hedging collars, 45V hydrogen. Targets 10% U.S. share growth.

4. Regarding overall performance highlights and key achievements, Q3 brought record results affirming our lead in solar, offshore wind, LDES amid decarbonization.

Revenue $1.45 billion, +28% YoY/+12% QoQ, beat guidance 5%, ninth double-digit quarter. FY24 raised to $5.6-5.8 billion (+32% from $4.2 billion 2023).

EBITDA $512 million, 35.3% margin (+420 bps), from 28% project margins via modules/IRA. FCF $420 million, net debt/EBITDA 1.2x, $150 million buyback, dividend +15% to $0.28/share.

Backlog 18.5 GW, $25 billion potential, 85% PPAs $42/MWh vs. $28 spot. 70% ITC-eligible, $4.2 billion credits.

Ops: 3.2 GW commissioned, including 1.2 GWdc Desert Bloom Arizona TOPCon at 32% factor via AI optimization, 98% uptime.

Offshore: 800 MW Hornsea Echo JV Orsted, 15 MW SG turbines, LCOE <£40/MWh.

Storage: 1.5 GWh, 500 MWh iron-air Texas LDES 100-hour 85% eff.

Fleet 12.4 GW, 8.2 TWh Q3 (+22% YoY), 95% RECs to Google/Microsoft 1.1 TWh premiums.

Achievements: Perovskite hybrid 28.5% lab eff at Intersolar with Oxford PV/Sumitomo, Q1 2025 pilots.

$1.8 billion GreenWave acquisition adds 4 GW BESS. 100 MW H2 JV Plug Power Rotterdam, Shell offtake.

Regions: NA 62% ($900M), EMEA 25% ($360M), APAC 13% ($190M) with 600 MW Australia tender.

Sustainability: Scope 1/2 -45% YoY, CDP A-List third year.

Ahead: Hybrids 60% 2025 pipeline, $2.5 billion M&A dry powder LDES/H2 for $1.7T IEA path. Shaping $500B BNEF investment.

5. For operating capacity in MW and generation output in GWh, at Q3 end, operating portfolio 6,450 MW, +18% YoY from 5,450 MW, +4% QoQ from 6,200 MW. Growth from 350 MW Gemini solar-storage Nevada, 250 MW Texas wind V150-6.0 MW, 150 MW Imperial Valley repower LONGi Hi-MO 7 23.3% eff.

By tech: Solar 3,800 MW (59%, +22% YoY), wind 2,100 MW (33%, +12% seq), storage 550 MW/1,100 MWh (8%, +40%).

Regions: U.S. 4,900 MW (76%, ERCOT 1,800 MW $50/MWh scarcity), Europe 1,100 MW (17%), Aus/APAC 450 MW (7%).

Generation 14,250 GWh Q3, +15% YoY from 12,400 GWh, +8% QoQ 13,200 GWh; annualized 57 TWh.

Blended CF 25.8% (+160 bps YoY, >SEIA/IRENA). Solar 1,950 GWh 23.1% CF (+70 bps, Mojave +5% irradiance, Ecoppia cleaning), wind 10,800 GWh 29.4% (+130 bps, 7.2 m/s Gulf, WindESCo), storage enables 450 GWh optimized $120/MWh peaks.

Exceeded guidance 3% despite Beryl; YTD 40,800 GWh for 55-57 TWh FY, $450M IRA credits, 9-11% IRRs.

Prioritizing repower/hybrid: 20% solar+BESS 30% CF equiv, UK 100 MW/200 MWh TNUoS. India 500 MW SECI.

Q4: 6,700 MW, 15,000-15,500 GWh 26-27% CF with 300 MW AZ CODs. 10 GW pipeline 70% advanced for data centers/H2.

Execution for 20% CAGR, 85% EBITDA margins.

6. On revenue and earnings growth analysis, Q3 revenue $1.28 billion, +48% YoY from $865 million, +12% seq from $1.14 billion Q2—10th double-digit quarter. H1 $2.42 billion +46% YoY; FY24 $5.6-5.8 billion (42-47% growth).

Segments: Solar mfg 52% $665M +55% YoY, 15.2 GWdc shipments +62%, 6.2 GW Texas TOPCon 23.5% eff 95% util, 68% bifacial $0.08/W prem, 28 GW backlog NextEra/Duke.

EPC/dev 28% $358M +42%, 9 GWdc incl 1.2 GW SunForge CA 75% for Q4, LCOE $28/MWh, 72% SW U.S.

BESS 15% $192M +72%, 4.8 GWh incl 1.2 GWh Orsted hybrids, AuroraPack 95% eff vs Tesla, Microsoft 2 GWh.

Emerging 5% $64M H2 +100% 50 MW PEM Plug Power, 45% margins DOE $7B.

Geo: NA 68% IRA $370/kWh storage/$12/mod, EMEA 22% +35% Spain/Germany, APAC 10% India rebound.

EBITDA $385M +52% 30.1% margin (+140 bps) $0.22/W cost to $0.31/W. GAAP NI $210M $0.72 EPS +50%, non-GAAP $0.81 beat. FCF $145M funds $300M capex.

Trends: 510 GW solar 2023, 580 GW 2024 BNEF; 140 GWh BESS WoodMac. Mitigated UFLPA 40% U.S. wafers.

Accel: $1.2B capex 5 GW perovskite 30%+, $500M M&A DG, U.S. Steel racking, 70% hedged $55/MWh.

Q3 guide $1.45-1.50B, FY EBITDA 29-31%. $12.5B backlog 4.2x.

7. Finally, strategic priorities and outlook: With Q3 revenue $420M +32% YoY, EBITDA $128M 30.5%, excited for Q4/FY25 scaling solar PV, offshore wind, LDES. 12 GW deployed since start, $4.8B backlog visibility.

Pillars: 1. U.S. IRA: Q4 1.2 GW SW hybrids like 450 MW Gemini NV +200 MWh LFP, Nevada Gigafab 80% domestic 45X. FY25 3.5 GW CAISO/ERCOT curtail -15%, LCOE $28/MWh. TX 40% backlog, PJM 800 MW hybrids.

2. Offshore: Q3 installs +45% 350 MW. U.S. East 600 MW NY/VA BOEM Siemens 15 MW floating -18% CAPEX. Q4 400 MW Empire first power $150M EPC. FY25 1.8 GW 35% margins. Europe 25% Dutch Borssele FID REPowerEU. $50B global 2025 IRENA, 12% edge.

3. LDES/GridFlex: VPP 1.5 GW 250 GWh Q3. Iron-air 100 MWh Form 85% $65/kWh. Q4/FY25 2.4 GWh incl 500 MWh CA cap-trade, MISO 4-hr $120k/MW-yr. Storage rev +55% $650M 32% margins DOE loans.

4. Emerging: India 300 MW Adani JV PLI, Indonesia 50 MW float PV $35/MWh. H2 MoU Plug 100 MW Aus wind H2Global 15% rev ROIC 12% 2026.

Q4 rev $460-480M +32%, EBITDA $140-150M 31%. FY24 $1.75-1.78B +28% FCF $320M. FY25 $2.3-2.5B +32% EBITDA $720-780M 31-32% 10% PTC/ITC. Backlog 70% 12-mo. Capex $350M 60% growth, $800M revolver $500M ATM. Special div $0.25, $300M buyback. Debt 1.2x $1.1B liquidity.

Risks: Permitting FAST-41 buffers, polysi -22% $7.5/kg 70% hedged. BNEF 25% CAGR. Utility focus 95% PPA.

Positioned 30%+ CAGR.

Now, I'll hand over the call to Sarah Chen to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. Our financial performance in the third quarter was outstanding. Revenue reached $1.45 billion, representing a 28% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production. Our gross margin expanded to 35.3%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $300 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $210 million, or $0.72 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are raising our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

I'll now turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss our project development activities.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. Our project development pipeline continues to expand, with 12.4 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making excellent progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, further contributing to our revenue and profitability. We are also actively pursuing strategic acquisitions and partnerships to accelerate our growth.

Lisa Wong, can you update us on our technological advancements?

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Mike. We are dedicated to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts are focused on developing advanced technologies that enhance the efficiency, reliability, and affordability of renewable energy systems. We have made significant breakthroughs in areas such as advanced solar panel technologies like perovskite tandems at 28.5% efficiency, energy storage solutions including iron-air long-duration systems, and smart grid technologies like AI-driven VPPs. We believe that these technologies will play a pivotal role in transforming the energy landscape.

Next, Emma Rodriguez will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Emma Rodriguez:
Thank you, Lisa. Sustainability is a core value at AeroSolar Renewables, and we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and contributing to a more sustainable future. We have established ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions—Scope 1 and 2 down 45% year-over-year—improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that advance sustainability, earning CDP A-List recognition for the third year.

Now, Tom Keller will provide operational highlights.

Tom Keller:
Thank you, Emma. Our operational performance remains strong. We are focused on optimizing our operations, improving efficiency, and ensuring the reliability of our renewable energy assets, with fleet capacity at 12.4 GW generating 8.2 TWh in Q3. We are implementing best practices in areas such as asset management, maintenance, and supply chain management, including AI O&M and robotic cleaning for 98% uptime. We are also investing in training and development to ensure that our employees have the skills and knowledge they need to succeed.

I'll turn it back to Jordan Hayes for closing remarks.

Jordan Hayes:
Thank you, Tom. To summarize, AeroSolar Renewables had an exceptional third quarter. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, our commitment to innovation, and our focus on sustainability will drive continued growth and success.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question at this time, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Jordan Hayes:
Thanks, Ben. International expansion is a key priority, comprising about 30% of our pipeline. In Australia, we're deploying 800 MW including Hornsdale expansions and NEM hybrids yielding high IRRs from FCAS. Europe sees strong offshore like Nordsee Breeze with Equinor and REPowerEU grants, plus UK Balancing Mechanism storage. Chile's Atacama solar-storage leverages lithium synergies, and we're entering India with 300 MW JV Adani for PLI subsidies and Indonesia floating PV. Piloting tax equity analogs in CfD/EEG regimes keeps leverage low. With $3.5 billion queued financings and hedges, we aim for 20% international revenue by 2026, outpacing U.S.-only peers while mitigating domestic queue risks.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
How are you addressing the challenge of intermittency associated with renewable energy sources?

Lisa Wong:
Great question, Maria. Intermittency is core to our tech roadmap. Our 2.3 GW / 9.2 GWh storage fleet, growing to 5 GW by 2025, pairs with hybrids—55% of pipeline—for 98% solar capture and 85% capacity factors. Nexus VPP AI aggregates 1.5 GW for dynamic stacking: arbitrage $45/MWh, frequency $12/MWh, black-start. LDES like iron-air pilots offer 100+ hours at 85% eff, half lithium costs. Degradation <1.5%, validated DNV. FERC reforms and co-location shave queues, positioning LCOE $32/MWh hybrids vs. standalone $45/MWh. We're ahead of curve for 40% VRE grids.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Can you discuss the impact of government subsidies and tax incentives on your profitability?

Sarah Chen:
Absolutely, David. IRA is transformative: stacking 50%+ ITC/PTC via domestic/energy community adders drove Q3 EBITDA margins to 35.3%. Tax equity monetized $850 million Q3—35% funding—at 6.5-8% yields, recycling equity. 45X on modules/components adds $12/module. PTC $27/MWh indexed. YTD $450 million credits lift IRRs 9-11%. Europe REPowerEU/CfD 40% capex grants, Australia LTAs/FCAS. Without IRA, margins 500 bps lower, but visibility 85% contracted mitigates policy risk. FY25 guidance assumes 10% extensions, sensitivity +$2/share per 100 MW accel.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Rachel Patel:
What are your expectations for electricity demand growth in the coming years?

Jordan Hayes:
Rachel, demand growth is explosive, led by AI data centers—hyperscalers like Google/Microsoft took 1.1 TWh RECs Q3 at premiums. BNEF sees 25% clean tech CAGR to 2030; U.S. needs 3.5 GW additions FY25 for ERCOT/CAISO peaks. Global 580 GW solar/140 GWh BESS 2024. We're positioned with 18.5 GW backlog, hybrids for 24/7 dispatch, $12.5B revenue potential at $42/MWh PPAs. Data center PPAs, H2 offtake, VRE mandates drive 32% FY25 growth, targeting 30%+ long-term as grids hit 40% renewables.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, there appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Jordan Hayes for any closing remarks.

Jordan Hayes:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of AeroSolar Renewables. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
